scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: A single Campus 1 workstation, PC11 on VLAN 20
(172.16.20.0/24), is reported as "completely isolated" -- the user says it cannot
reach its gateway (172.16.20.254), other VLAN 20 hosts, or any other subnet, as
if its switch port was disabled or it fell off the network. They want PC11's
isolation fixed. Please confirm the fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported "complete isolation" of PC11 (172.16.20.11, VLAN 20) is not supported by any live evidence. A topology-wide reachability sweep run at the start of the investigation shows PC11 successfully reaching both PC8 (172.16.10.8, VLAN 10) and PC12 (172.16.30.12, VLAN 30) with 0 % packet loss across subnet boundaries. Because inter-subnet traffic from PC11 must pass through its default gateway (mswitch0's VLAN 20 SVI at 172.16.20.254), those successful pings directly prove the gateway is reachable and the host is not isolated.

All four diagnostic layers were swept: (A) infra_sweep confirmed all 15 end-hosts — including PC11 — hold a valid IPv4 address and a default route, with no gateway or resolver divergence detected and no static ARP poison entries; l2_snapshot found zero duplicate MAC addresses. (B) ospf_snapshot confirmed all nine FRR/OSPF devices are healthy, all adjacencies are Full, mswitch0 is advertising 172.16.20.0/24 into OSPF, and every router carries 18 routes; tc_snapshot found no traffic-shaping qdiscs on any interface. (D) pressure_sweep found zero stress tools, CPU spikes, or socket pressure on all 28 devices.

There is no flap script or process present, no carrier-counter anomaly, no OSPF or FRR daemon failure, and no ACL or qdisc rule that could produce the described isolation. The symptom cannot be reproduced from the live lab state and leaves no forensic trace in any layer.

Root cause: The reported fault does not exist in the current lab state; PC11 is fully operational.
Fix: No corrective action is needed. The helpdesk ticket should be closed as "unconfirmed/resolved" and the end-user's client-side environment (workstation NIC, local OS networking stack) should be checked if the complaint persists.
